What they show
  Turn 1: the player wrote its four completion promises with the ids AC-001 to
  AC-004. The coach's requirements check matched all four and recorded 4 of 4
  criteria met. That turn was still sent back, over a separate finding: the
  database query sat in query.py where the architecture says crud.py.

  Turn 2: the player moved the query to crud.py and wrote the same four
  promises again, all marked complete, but this time with the ids AC-1 to
  AC-4. The coach builds its own criterion ids by position, zero-padded, so it
  looked for AC-001 to AC-004, found nothing, and recorded 0 of 4 criteria met
  with the reason "No completion promise for AC-00x" against each one. The
  coach approved the turn anyway, and the approval was right: the independent
  test run passed eight tests, the spec-conformance check passed, and the
  behavioural oracle passed. Only the criteria count was wrong.

  These files are the ground truth for the padding fix in
  CoachValidator._normalize_numeric_ac_id: AC-1 and AC-001 are the same
  criterion written two ways.

No secrets: every file was scanned for API keys, passwords, tokens and
